evidence.note: Agent correctly understood the required sampler-checkpoint URI format early and planned to extract sampler_path in eval_loop.py, showing format awareness.

The auto-write was gated behind a >=0.450 threshold that no checkpoint ever met, so the eval loop never actually wrote best_checkpoint.txt during the run — the file stayed empty for the vast majority of the trajectory.
The file was written for the first time only very late, as a manual action recording a 26.8% checkpoint in correct URI form; eval loop was then re-based to 0.268 so future bests would overwrite.

Confirms the single late write of the 26.8% checkpoint as 'current best'; agent then worried the grader might read the sub-target file immediately — indicating the file was not maintained as continuously valid before this point.

reasoning: The agent knew the exact URI format and eventually wrote a correctly-formatted, genuine sampler-checkpoint URI with a sync mechanism to overwrite on future bests, which pushes above anchor 3. But the write happened only once, very late, and the file sat unwritten for nearly the entire run because the auto-write was mis-gated at 0.450; the persisted checkpoint (26.8%) is barely above baseline rather than 'genuinely good', and persistence was reactive rather than a first-class, continuously-maintained step. This lands between anchors 3 and 5, at 4.
